CHATGPT REFUSED TO COPY STEPHEN KING'S 'EXACT STYLE'
slides.body: When Ars Technica asked ChatGPT for a story intro in Stephen King's style, it said it "can't write in Stephen King's exact style" but offered text that "captures a similar feeling." It gave the same refusal for J.K. Rowling and Amy Tan

slides.headline: DEAD AUTHORS ARE STILL FAIR GAME
slides.body: An analysis by No Latency found ChatGPT blocked style requests for living authors but still complied for dead ones like Dickens and Hemingway. Ars Technica's own tests got refusals for both — the behavior appears to still be shifting

slides.headline: AUTHORS SUED OPENAI OVER ITS 'UNCANNY' COPYING ABILITY
slides.body: Multiple book authors have sued OpenAI, with one case citing ChatGPT's "uncanny ability" to match copyrighted work. A George Washington University law professor told Bloomberg Law that no technology has ever copied personal style this well or this cheaply

slides.headline: OPENAI PULLED A CHATGPT FEATURE AND NOBODY GOT WARNED
slides.body: If your business writes emails or social posts with ChatGPT, OpenAI just proved they can change what it does without asking. The businesses that won't feel this run AI built around their own voice — set up once, works the same way every day, no one else controls the switch
